title: What happens when the server is killed

columns.crash.dbos-resume: Killed inside a template leg on DBOS

notes: Each entry is what that cell's test required and saw in this run. Of these cells, only the template leg on DBOS resumes; a flow leg killed on the builtin engine fails, and so does its pipeline. What each cell checks, where this holds, and what no cell tests: [What happens when the server is killed](./benchmark/README.md#what-happens-when-the-server-is-killed).

crash.gate.crashed: The server process, with SIGKILL, running the `hello-crash/slow-publish` pipeline.
crash.gate.when: While the `review` person gate waits for a decision, after the three legs before it have finished.
crash.gate.required: The gate is still waiting after the restart and no finished leg has a new run. Approving it finishes the pipeline with one run per leg and one published artifact.
crash.gate.how: A person gate has no Run: it is a step waiting in the pipeline's stored record, with no process behind it. ADR-0125's liveness check judges leg Runs, so it has nothing to judge here.

crash.mid-leg.crashed: The server process, with SIGKILL, running the `hello-crash/slow-publish` pipeline.
crash.mid-leg.when: About a second into the `slow` flow leg on the builtin engine, after the leg's engine handle is saved.
crash.mid-leg.required: Right after the restart the leg is still `running` on the same run. Within 90 s it settles `failed` on that run, with an engine error saying the job was lost and a new owner recorded. The pipeline fails, the leg gets no new run, the `stage` and `publish` legs after it never start, and no artifact is staged or published. The work isn't resumed.
crash.mid-leg.how: ADR-0125 D3 calls a dead owner's lock found free once undetermined, and a second check more than one re-acquire interval later says the owner is dead; D4 then re-attaches the leg. Settling `failed` comes from the builtin engine, whose job table died with the old process, and isn't an ADR-0125 outcome. The harness signals only the server process, so the leg's engine subprocess isn't killed with it.

crash.dbos-resume.column: Killed inside a template leg on DBOS
crash.dbos-resume.crashed: The server process, with SIGKILL, running the `hello-cairn/ask-the-docs` pipeline.
crash.dbos-resume.when: While the `assistant` template leg, a DBOS workflow, waits on its model call.
crash.dbos-resume.required: Before the kill the run names no in-process owner and its workflow is `PENDING`. After the restart the model is called again, the same run finishes `done`, its workflow reads `SUCCESS`, and the pipeline reaches its person gate. Approving it finishes the pipeline with one run per leg.
crash.dbos-resume.how: ADR-0125 D1 leaves a durable runtime's liveness to that runtime, so this recovery isn't an ADR-0125 outcome. DBOS runs a `PENDING` workflow again at boot, and the LangGraph checkpointer decides where the graph picks up.

not_covered: The Temporal runtime. No cell runs it: the cells run on the in-process runtime and on DBOS.

Whether a node's side effects repeat. A node running at the kill runs again, which the DBOS integration leaves to operator idempotency. No cell shows that side effects aren't repeated or that earlier nodes are skipped.
A kill inside a task leg, or inside a template leg on the in-process runtime.
A kill while a template run is parked on its own approval (on DBOS, at `recv`).
A kill inside a flow leg before its engine handle is saved.
A flow leg on an engine whose jobs outlive the server, such as Metaflow or SkyPilot. Every cell uses the builtin engine, so no cell shows a re-attached leg finishing.
What the leg's engine subprocess goes on to do after its leg is marked `failed`.
A kill while a scheduled or event step fires, while a finalizer runs, after a cancel, or while a pipeline starts. A cell tests only the moment its column names.
More than one server: a second replica, or a server on another host.
Anything other than the server process dying. Postgres and the disk stay up in every cell, so a Postgres restart, a failover or a power loss is not tested.
How fast recovery is. A cell only has a time limit.
